body: Learn why 20,630 xg on a 20 kg unit matters for molecular biology work.

Molecular biology protocols often need genuinely high g-force for pelleting nucleic acids or precipitates, but not the volume that comes with a general-purpose centrifuge. Model 3300 delivers 20,630 xg, well into research-grade force territory, from a unit that weighs only 20 kg and fits comfortably on a bench already crowded with PCR machines and pipette racks.

sections.title: Built for Plates, Nothing Else
sections.tabSummary: Why a dedicated rotor changes plate-based throughput
body: Learn why a dedicated rotor changes plate-based throughput on the Kubota Plate Spin 3.

Most centrifuges treat plate handling as one option among several, a plate rotor that competes for slot time with tube-based rotors, and has to be swapped in and out. Plate Spin 3 removes that trade-off entirely: the plate rotor is equipped with the main unit, not sold or configured separately, so a lab running plate-based work exclusively never spends time on a rotor decision at all.

That focus pays off directly in capacity. 6 microplates, or 2 × 96-hole PCR plates, or 2 deep well plates, cover the three formats a high-throughput screening or PCR workflow actually needs, without diluting the design to also handle standard tubes.

sections.title: Twenty Rotors Across Five Geometries
sections.description: Learn why the Kubota Model 6200 is genuinely the broadest centrifuge in this Kubota range.
paragraphs: Model 6200 covers five distinct rotor geometries on one unit: 1 multi rotor, 4 multiple swinging bucket rotors, 5 micro rotors, 8 angle rotors, and 2 micro-plate rotors. That's more rotor options than Model 6000 (15) and more geometry types than any other Kubota model built so far, the "multi rotor" category doesn't appear anywhere else in this set.

sections.title: Model 6200 Against the High-Speed Range
sections.tabSummary: Where it sits relative to Model 6000 and 7000
body: Where it sits relative to Model 6000 and Model 7000.

Model 6200 trades some raw top-end speed and RCF for genuinely broader rotor coverage. Model 6000 and Model 7000 both reach 22,000 rpm, ahead of Model 6200's 16,000 rpm, and Model 7000's 52,490 xg dwarfs Model 6200's 23,470 xg. But Model 6200 covers a sample range neither of the other two states directly, down to 0.2 mL PCR tubes, and carries more total rotor options than Model 6000 (20 against 15).

heroParagraphs: Model 6200 is Kubota's own "Universal Refrigerated Centrifuge," and the rotor count backs that framing up: 1 multi rotor, 4 multiple swinging bucket rotors, 5 micro rotors, 8 angle rotors, and 2 micro-plate rotors, 20 options across five distinct geometries, the widest set built in this Kubota range yet.
